svg.aria-label: How to write 重: 9 strokes · 8 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 重
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 重 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 重.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E9%87%8D.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 重. Medians 1–2 draw the top as 千 opens: a short left-falling stroke, then the long horizontal; medians 3–6 draw the box of 田 as 里 does: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom; median 7 draws the long vertical from the top stroke down through the box; medians 8–9 draw the two horizontals of 土 on it, the lower one longer. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
